title: Computer-use and browser agents
summary: A model looks at screenshots and drives a browser or desktop by clicking and typing, or by writing automation code. It reaches software with no API, and it reads untrusted screen content while holding the controls.
useIf: A task lives behind a user interface that has no API or MCP tool, and you can run the agent in an isolated environment with confirmations.
avoidIf: An API, MCP tool or script already does the job, or the environment holds sensitive data or logged-in sessions the agent should not reach.

explain.md: In **computer use** the model sees screenshots and other tool results, decides what to do next, and your application executes the action. You provide the environment: the model does not run anything itself [[r36]]. The loop is screenshot, action, screenshot, bounded by a step limit.

explain.title: Computer-use loop with a policy gate
explain.alt: A screenshot goes to the model, which proposes an action. A policy gate checks the allow-list and asks for confirmation on consequential steps. Approved actions run in a sandbox, which produces a new screenshot.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  S[Screenshot] --> M[Model]
  M --> P[Proposed action]
  P --> G{Policy gate}
  G -->|allowed| X[Run in sandbox]
  G -->|consequential| H[Human confirm]
  H --> X
  X --> S

explain.md: The gate is where you enforce policy. The model proposes an action, but your code decides whether it runs: it checks the target against an allow-list, asks a person to confirm anything consequential such as paying, deleting or sending, and stops the run when a step or time budget is spent. The model never holds the keyboard directly.

explain.caption: Vendor paths, checked 2026-10-13
head: Vendor
Path
Status and notes
rows: Code execution (model writes Playwright or PyAutoGUI scripts) or the `computer` tool with structured mouse and keyboard actions
For GPT-6 Astra OpenAI recommends code execution. The `computer` tool stays supported. If you already expose UI operations as function or remote MCP tools, you can keep that [[r36]]
`computer_toolset_20260801` client toolset (17 member tools), plus a separate browser use tool for web-only tasks
GA on the Claude API and Google Cloud, beta on Microsoft Foundry and Bedrock. Claude 5.5 and later reject `computer_20251124` and `computer_20250124` on the Claude API [[r35]]
`computer-use-preview` model, screenshot and action loop in a VM or sandbox
Preview, no SLA, not recommended for production, access by application form, not supported in network-isolated Foundry [[r34]] [[r27]]

explain.md: **Safe use** follows the same checklist across vendors: isolate the environment, allow-list sites and apps, treat screen content as untrusted input, confirm consequential actions and bound the number of steps [[r36]]. Foundry's page warns of prompt injection risk and advises running on a VM or sandbox with no access to sensitive data [[r34]]. Prefer an API or MCP tool when one exists, and prefer code execution or a browser-only tool over full desktop control for web tasks.

whereToUse: Back-office or legacy applications with no API where manual data entry is the only route
Testing user flows and filling forms in staging environments
Web research and form tasks, ideally through browser automation in an isolated browser
Prototyping automation before an API or integration is built

use: No API or MCP tool exists and the work is repetitive enough to automate
The agent runs in a VM or sandbox with no sensitive data or personal sessions
Consequential actions (submit, pay, delete, send) need human confirmation
avoid: Running on a person's own logged-in desktop or browser profile
Production workloads that need an SLA while using a preview tool
Environments with network isolation on Foundry, where the tool is unsupported
flips: An API or MCP tool appears: switch to it, since it is faster, cheaper and safer
Web-only task: use browser automation code instead of pixel-level desktop control
Your vendor retires a tool version: update the tool name, as Claude 5.5 and later reject the older versions

pitfalls.symptom: The agent clicks something it was never asked to do
pitfalls.cause: Screen text or a page carried instructions and the model treated them as commands (prompt injection)
pitfalls.fix: Treat screen content as untrusted, allow-list targets, confirm consequential actions and keep the environment free of sensitive data.

pitfalls.symptom: The run loops for a long time and costs a lot
pitfalls.cause: No step cap, or the page changed and the agent keeps retrying
pitfalls.fix: Bound steps, set time budgets and stop with a clear failure state.

pitfalls.symptom: Calls start failing after a model upgrade
pitfalls.cause: The older tool version is rejected by newer models, for example `computer_20251124` on Claude 5.5 and later
pitfalls.fix: Pin tool versions to the model and run a smoke test on every upgrade.

scenarios.title: Legacy desktop app, no API
scenarios.situation: Staff re-key about 200 records a day into a legacy desktop application with no API. Data is internal and moderately sensitive. Mistakes are fixable but costly.
unknowns: Can the app run in a VM with a service account?
scenarios.question: How do you automate it?

options.name: Run the agent on an employee's logged-in desktop
options.why: It exposes personal sessions and data to an agent reading untrusted screen content.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only on a dedicated throwaway machine with no personal access.

options.name: Scripted RPA
options.tradeoff: Breaks on UI changes and cannot handle variations.

options.name: Computer use in a dedicated VM, with an allow-list, a step limit and confirmation before submit
options.why: It follows the safety checklist: isolate, allow-list, bound steps and confirm consequential actions.
options.tradeoff: Slow loop and setup effort, and you still sample outputs for errors.

flips.then: Keep a human on every submit.

scenarios.takeaway: No API does not mean no controls. Isolate, allow-list and confirm.

scenarios.title: Web research and form filling
scenarios.situation: An agent gathers pricing from public sites and fills a quote form on one partner site. Everything is web based and no credentials are involved for the research part.
unknowns: Is the partner form behind a login?
scenarios.question: Which approach fits?

options.name: Code execution driving an isolated browser
options.why: OpenAI recommends code execution for GPT-6 Astra, and scripts can combine actions and loops in one call for web tasks.
options.tradeoff: Needs a sandboxed runtime and script review.

options.name: Full desktop control on an admin workstation
options.why: It gives a web-reading agent a machine with broad access.
options.tradeoff: Right only for a native app that has no browser route, and then in a VM.

options.name: The pixel-level computer tool in a VM
options.tradeoff: Slower, more screenshots and more tokens than scripted browser control.

flips.then: Add credential isolation and confirmation before submit.

scenarios.takeaway: For web tasks, scripted browser control beats full desktop control.

scenarios.title: Production target with an SLA
scenarios.situation: A team wants computer use in production. Their contract demands a supported service with an SLA. They are evaluating the Foundry tool.
unknowns: Is a GA path available in their cloud?
scenarios.question: How do you proceed?

options.name: Ship the Foundry computer use tool
options.why: It is preview with no SLA and not recommended for production.
options.tradeoff: Fine for a proof of concept and for learning the loop.

options.name: Use a GA path such as Claude's `computer_toolset_20260801` on the Claude API, or code execution, in your own sandbox
options.why: The Claude toolset is GA on the Claude API and the sandbox is under your control.
options.tradeoff: A different vendor surface to secure, and you check data and residency terms.

options.name: Wait for a GA Foundry tool
options.tradeoff: No automation until then, and the sources checked give no GA date.

flips.if: Network isolation on Foundry is also required
flips.then: Computer use is unsupported there. Use a separate, controlled sandbox.

scenarios.takeaway: Check the status label before production. Preview means no SLA.

quiz.q: For GPT-6 Astra, what integration does OpenAI recommend for computer use?
options: Use the `computer` tool only, with structured mouse and keyboard actions
Code execution with Playwright or PyAutoGUI
quiz.explain: OpenAI recommends code execution for GPT-6 Astra, and the `computer` tool remains supported as an alternative.

quiz.q: Which controls belong in a computer-use deployment?
options: Isolate the environment in a VM or sandbox
Treat on-screen text as trusted instructions
Confirm consequential actions and bound steps
quiz.explain: Isolation, allow-lists, confirmation and step bounds are the standard checklist. Screen content is untrusted input and must not be treated as instructions.

quiz.q: A Foundry project uses network isolation. Can the Foundry computer use tool run there as of 2026-10-13?
options: Yes, once a private endpoint is configured on the project
No, computer use is not supported under isolation
quiz.explain: Browser automation and computer use are not supported in network-isolated Foundry. Private endpoints, CMK and the Standard setup do not change that.

flashcards.back: Screenshot, model proposes an action, your app executes it in an isolated environment, new screenshot. Bound it with a step limit and confirmations.

flashcards.front: What is the status of the Foundry computer use tool?
flashcards.back: Preview, no SLA, not recommended for production, access by application form, unsupported under network isolation (checked 2026-10-13).

flashcards.front: What do Claude 5.5 and later do with old computer tool versions?
flashcards.back: They reject `computer_20251124` and `computer_20250124` on the Claude API. Use `computer_toolset_20260801`, GA on the Claude API.
